scope: Independent epoch semantics and fixed-bound candidate evaluation; no implementation approval or film approval

sources.claim: Screencast metadata records a frame-swap timestamp typed as Network.TimeSinceEpoch.

The time-origin timestamp relates the monotonic origin to the estimated Unix epoch; adding relative performance time produces epoch-relative time. The specification explicitly notes possible divergence from current wall-clock time after adjustments.

conclusion: The visible marker displacement does not isolate a clock offset. The marker is timestamped before rendering/compositing and becomes visible later. Subtracting this displacement from every capture PTS can shift native intervals incorrectly. Direct epoch-space comparison needs separately measured clock agreement; first/last request-round-trip brackets can supply that evidence for new takes.
probeRequirements: Record host request-start and response-receipt epochs and page performance epoch for start/end probes.
Treat the page-to-host offset as an interval bounded by each round trip.
Require sufficient agreement/stability to test endpoint residuals against the same fixed budget across the whole possible offset interval. Do not add probe uncertainty to a tolerance.
Keep missing, wide, inconsistent, or moving clock evidence inconclusive.
